items.title: Jack Teagarden Interview, 1959-10-29
items.q: Yeah, I met him here on some of the trips here.

ctx.x: And who was with you after that?

Oh, Terry Shand and, uh, and, uh, let's see. Terry, Terry Shand and I, we came and joined another band there, and it was called Youngberg Marin. It was about a nine or ten piece band. It was hotel work. But there was a band over at the Washington Hotel called, uh, the Louisiana Ramblers, Tim Kelly, and, uh, some, he's still in Louisiana, or Mississippi, Jackson, Mississippi, I think. And, uh, Pat and Bobby Dequeer, the boys, one played trumpet and one trombone, they were very good. But they weren't from…
Let's see. Uh, hold on. I hate to get started on anything. We'll just let it run off, huh, Paul? Yeah. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: It was always experimenting, like Jack Teagarden, you know, always experimenting.

ctx.x: Uh, but he covered a lot of ground in, in those years, and he used to make it, he made his own mop pieces. He, he worked in the, machine shop, and his, his, his brother, uh, today is head of this Bishop Edel machine company here, and he wanted him to be a machinist. Emmett didn't care about machinists, he, he wanted to play music. So he'd work all day in the fountain, and he made, he made his own mouth pieces. It was always experimenting, like Jack Teagarden, you know, always experimenting. I think he had a…
Tell more about Emmett, um, how he got, did he ever tell you how he got started on the cornet? Did he use cornet or trumpet?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: And they worked at the hotel and used to get off at one o'clock, so Jack and I would run up and get ahead of a bunch of these underground places

ctx.x: by the name of Jack Pettis, and we used to run across Louis every once in a while, you know. Let's take one more break here, and then we'll come back and listen to some more from that album, and also some old Duke Ellington that's kind of interesting. We'll be back on jazz review after this word. Now, a few words about the Sony 250A tape deck. Forget it. Forget about leaving it on. The 250A turns itself off when the reel is finished, or if the tape breaks. Forget about overheating and burnt tubes. Because the…

much about the Ellington band at the Cotton Club? Yeah, I used to go up there quite a bit because at that time everything was in Harlem. You know, there wasn't anything. They had big clubs downtown, but there was no jazz downtown in New York at all, and everything was in Harlem. And Jack Teegarden was playing with Benny Pollock. And they worked at the hotel and used to get off at one o'clock, so Jack and I would run up and get ahead of a bunch of these underground places, Budbee's and Susie's and all the way…
